svg.title: Kath-kuni — a wall built to move
svg.desc: Cutaway of a kath-kuni wall corner showing alternating courses of dry-laid stone and paired deodar beams, with an inset plan of one timber course showing the two beams, the rubble infill, the cross-tie and the interlocked corner.
svg.text: Kath-kuni — a wall built to move
Wood and stone in alternating courses, no mortar and no metal. Kāshth, wood; kona, corner.
a pair of deodar beams, one to each face
the beams interlock at the corner,
as the wall rises, stone gives way to wood
No mortar, no nails, no steel. The wall is held down by its own weight, so in a tremor it can shear a little, grind, and settle back.
Concrete cannot do that. Sarahan's Bhimakali temple — your first night — is the great surviving example, and it is still standing.
